name: 3sixteen
why: Denim, shirts and boots from New York, with two stores of its own, cut from named Japanese and Portuguese mills, with its boots made in Northampton, England.
origin: Founded in 2003 (press: The Hobbyist interview with Andrew Chen, 13 Mar 2025; brand About page says only 'over two decades ago') in New York City (press: Wikipedia; brand About page does not state a place) by Andrew Chen with a friend not named (press: The Hobbyist) and Johan Lam named co-owner (press: Wikipedia) and brand About page names no founders.

craft_evidence.owned: None found: About page and Hobbyist interview describe outside factories; no owned factory, mill or workshop stated
craft_evidence.makers: Sanders & Sanders, Northampton England (bench-made loafer, derbies, boots; product pages); Tanner Goods, Portland OR (leather patches, About page); no factory named on clothing pages (Knit polo says only 'partner factory in Peru')
craft_evidence.mills: Nihon Menpu, Okayama Japan (denim, RS-105x page: 'Woven in Okayama, Japan by Nihon Menpu exclusively for 3sixteen'); Kuroki Mills, Okayama (About page, custom denim); Albano Morgado (wool suiting, Pleated Trouser page)
craft_evidence.madein: 12 of 12 product pages read state a place: 11 name a country (USA jeans; Portugal x3; India x2; Peru x3 'Knit in Peru'; England x2) and the tee names cities only (knit Los Angeles, cut/sewn San Francisco); wash/care not given
craft_evidence.heritage: Partly dated, loosely placed: About says 'Founded over two decades ago' and 'modern history began in 2008' with no founding place or founders; press (Hobbyist, 13 Mar 2025) dates first tees to summer 2003
craft_evidence.process: Denim only: 15.75oz raw indigo selvedge, 3x1 weave, sanforized, skewed, lightly singed; Goodyear welt and bench-made on footwear; tee 270GSM combed cotton, laundered to reduce shrinkage; little process detail elsewhere
craft_evidence.reasoning: Names its cloth mills (Nihon Menpu, Kuroki, Albano Morgado) and its shoe maker (Sanders & Sanders, Northampton) and states a country on every page read, but owns no facility and names no clothing factory; process is documented for denim only. Fits a 3 (names makers and mills, owns nothing); an owned facility would be needed for a 4.

ownership.owner: Private; co-owned by Andrew Chen and Johan Lam (press: Wikipedia, The Hobbyist); brand does not state ownership

opview: “We just wanted to try and add our voice to the mix and see if we could make something that people would want to buy.” — Andrew Chen, co-owner, The Hobbyist #7: An Interview with 3sixteen Co-Owner Andrew Chen (Will Schube, The Hobbyist, Substack)
